note:
The widget set grew from 39 to 51 in three days because nothing owned the total, and every one of the twelve passed its own admission review honestly. Rulesets will grow faster: they are data, so adding one costs no code, no release build and no lab check. The same failure is therefore available one layer down, and this file is here before the layer is finished rather than after.

But the constraint must be a different one, and copying the widget rule would be a mistake. A widget must be GENERAL -- that is what widgets/standardization.json enforces, and it is why twelve example-specific widgets were a problem. A ruleset must be PARTICULAR: knowledge about a place, a disease, a published hierarchy, is exactly what this layer exists to hold, and refusing an example-specific ruleset would refuse the point of it.

What a ruleset can be wrong about is its authority. So the ratchet counts rulesets with no cited basis. Declaring the three shipped rulesets as data is what made that countable: two of three carry a disclaimer where a citation would go -- 'Threshold is illustrative', 'not a clinical recommendation or routed travel time'. Both are honest. Neither is a source. The count may fall freely and may never rise.

Restructured 2026-10-12, on the practitioner's rule that each ruleset-based widget must be able to map to evidence and provenance -- a PDF or a URL. A ruleset's basis now carries EvidenceReference values of the same url-or-pdf-with-digest shape node references use, so a cited PDF is verified by hash rather than trusted by filename, and the provenance emitter already knew how to write it. That change immediately weakened the earlier count: the one ruleset recorded as having a cited basis cites three papers as author-year strings, which resolve to nothing a reader can open. So the ratchet counts rulesets with no RESOLVABLE evidence, which is three of three, not one of three. No locator was invented to close the gap -- the gap is recorded, with what would resolve each entry. Two 2.0.0 versions published 2026-10-12 for PORT TYPE changes rather than rule changes: nb06-evidence emits a point layer instead of the gradedFacilities stud, and access-review consumes distances instead of the `access` port type. The rules and the conclusions are identical in both; 1.0.0 is kept in each case because a saved workflow pinned it, and because a rule change changes results while a port type change changes connections.

uncited.whatWouldResolveIt: A published or practitioner-agreed distance threshold for outreach review, with the population and setting it was derived for, added as a url or pdf evidence reference. Nothing is named at all today, resolvable or otherwise.

uncited.statedBy: The ruleset text itself: "not a clinical recommendation or routed travel time."
uncited.whatWouldResolveIt: Sources for the review threshold in minutes and for the 5, 15 and 30 minute zone bounds. Three uncited numbers, not one: the bounds are literals in the rules rather than parameters, because they are this rulesets own banding.

uncited.whatWouldResolveIt: A DOI, publisher URL or digested PDF for each of Baik 2019, Mokomane 2024 and Dickinson 2017. This is the ruleset that looked cited and is not: three author-year strings are what the project holds, and they open nothing.

uncited.statedBy: The ruleset text itself: "Not a judgement that large is wrong."
uncited.whatWouldResolveIt: Nothing, as shipped, and that is deliberate -- this ruleset exists to answer a question about the machinery, not about extents. It resolves by being REPLACED: if rules over derived geometry turn out to be useful, the one that proves it will be a particular ruleset about a particular question, with a size that matters for that question and a source for it. If experiment 113 concludes against the approach, this is deleted and the ceiling returns to 3.

ceilingRaisedTo4: Raised from 3 on 2026-10-14, with the reason the ledger asks for. Experiment 113 tests whether a ruleset can run over a quantity DERIVED from geometry rather than over an imported column, and no existing ruleset takes polygons -- so the question cannot be asked without adding one. The cost is exactly what this ledger exists to resist: a fourth uncited ruleset, added because it was cheap. It is recorded as a debt against the experiment rather than as a new normal. If 113 concludes the approach is not worth having, deleting extent-review returns the ceiling to 3 in the same commit; if it is worth having, the ruleset that replaces this one must be sourced.
ceilingPolicy: Clarified by the practitioner on 2026-10-14, after the ceiling was raised 3 -> 4 for experiment 113: "OK with ceiling, we move up a little or down both OK, not too much." So this ceiling is NOT a one-way ratchet like the widget budget or the naming count. It may move in either direction, by a little, with the reason recorded in the same commit. What it exists to stop is unnoticed growth -- rulesets are data, so adding one costs no code, no release build and no lab check, and the widget set grew 39 -> 51 in three days for exactly that reason. A ceiling that can move by one with a stated reason still makes the fourth uncited ruleset a decision someone made, which is the whole purpose. A jump of several at once is what the policy refuses.
ceilingRaisedTo5: RAISED AND LOWERED THE SAME DAY, 2026-10-26, and the round trip is the record worth keeping. It went to 5 when extract-contract was written, carrying the AR6 contract that slr_extract_import had held in TypeScript with its three citations named and unresolvable. The practitioner then said the thing that mattered: "the citations are also DOIs, so when transmitted and embedded in the output they are independently verifiable." They are, and all three were resolved against the public DOI system on 2026-10-17 (docs/research/doi-resolution-probe-2026-10-17.md) -- the chapter as a book-chapter, FACTS as a journal-article, the dataset as a dataset returning version 20210809. Attached as resolvable evidence, extract-contract stops being uncited and the ceiling returns to 4 with ONE MORE RULESET THAN BEFORE. It is also the first ruleset of five to carry resolvable evidence at all.
